motivation: Pooled pre-loss Thalassia history predicts re-recording, while the effect disappears in bare loss states. Decompose local history into current focal-species persistence and pre-existing generic seagrass habitat continuity to test whether the recovery signal is focal-specific or mainly a persistent microsite property.

history_decomposition.thalassia_run: immediately consecutive consensus years ending in source year with Thalassia present
history_decomposition.any_seagrass_run: immediately consecutive consensus years ending in source year with any seagrass present
history_decomposition.habitat_headstart: any_seagrass_run - thalassia_run; number of continuous vegetated years preceding the current continuous Thalassia run

primary_hypothesis.statement: Within stable transects, current continuous Thalassia run length retains a positive association with one-year re-recording after controlling for pre-focal habitat headstart, community-continuity state, and source mixture.
primary_hypothesis.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the centered Thalassia-run coefficient > 0

secondary.habitat_headstart_term: report centered habitat-headstart coefficient and bootstrap interval descriptively
secondary.predictor_structure: report distribution of Thalassia run, any-seagrass run, and habitat headstart

interpretation.supported: Focal-species persistence history carries recovery information beyond generic pre-existing vegetation continuity, consistent with a Thalassia-specific local legacy signal.
interpretation.unsupported: Once generic habitat continuity history is represented, focal-species run length no longer adds robust recovery information; the earlier local-legacy signal is better interpreted as persistent microsite/habitat quality.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc history decomposition on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
A focal-specific coefficient would still not prove clonal memory or residual rhizomes without below-ground measurements.
A habitat-headstart coefficient would not identify which environmental property makes the microsite persistent.
Return is recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not change the history decomposition, node-centering, controls, model, minima, or support threshold after opening the joint-history endpoint.
